channel.title: Block Club Chicago - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Block Club Chicago (blockclubchicago.org)

item.title: Rise Training Academy Brings Martial Arts, Dance Classes To Auburn Gresham
item.description: The Black and Filipina co-owned studio on the South Side offers classes in West African dance, martial arts like jiu-jitsu and Capoeira, and more.

item.title: Fewer Chicago School-Aged Kids Are Enrolled In City’s Public Schools, New Analysis Finds
item.description: A report from the advocacy group Kids First Chicago found that the district’s “market share” has slipped from 75 percent to 71 percent since 2018.

item.title: Lurie Children’s Halts Gender-Affirming Meds For New Patients Under 18 Amid Federal Threats
item.description: The Downtown hospital’s decision comes after the Trump administration said it was referring Lurie and five other hospitals in five states for a federal investigation.

item.title: North Center Senior Center Slated For Closure Will Stay Open, But Questions Remain
item.description: Catholic Charities reversed course on its plan to close the North Center Senior Satellite Center March 31, but gave few details about the decision to neighbors and Ald. Matt Martin.

item.title: It Will Feel Like 35 Below Zero In Chicago During Weekend Cold Snap
item.description: The extreme cold is expected to last through early next week, with dangerously cold wind chills bringing frostbite risk this weekend.

item.title: Broadway Hit ‘Oh, Mary!’ Coming To Chicago As Part Of Nationwide Tour
item.description: The acclaimed dark comedy written by Cole Escola follows alcoholic Mary Todd Lincoln leading up to Abraham Lincoln's assassination. Casting is yet to be announced.

item.title: 3 People Charged After Weekend Police Chase Through Beverly, Morgan Park Ends In Crash
item.description: Three people were arrested in Morgan Park Sunday in connection to an Evergreen Park car burglary that led officers on a chase into the 19th Ward, including a crash on Western Avenue.

item.title: Congress Theater Gets OK To Apply For $25 Million Loan For Long-Awaited Overhaul
item.description: City Council approved an ordinance authorizing the federal loan application, which city officials plan to submit next week.

item.title: Youth Curfew Vote Delayed After Mayor’s Office, Downtown Alder Reach Compromise
item.description: The substitute proposal would formalize existing police powers to disperse disruptive gatherings while banning snap curfews. It could go in front of City Council in February.

item.title: City Council Passes Ban On Intoxicating Hemp Products — Except THC Drinks — As Mayor Weighs Veto
item.description: The ban would force businesses to take intoxicating hemp products like edibles, flower and vapes off shelves by April 1, but it makes exemptions for THC drinks and CBD creams.
